To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) photometric calibration is crucial to accurately evaluate tracking accuracy and (2) DSO performs better than ORB-SLAM, especially on sequences with wide field-of-view cameras.

the tracking accuracy of ORB-SLAM is on average 2.6% of the distance traveled (1.2% for the best sequence, 5.3% for the worst), and that DSO performs better than ORB-SLam for all sequences except the one with the highest tracking accuracy.

the tracking accuracy of visual odometry and visual SLAM algorithms is highly dependent on camera motion direction, that the tracking accuracy is also dependent on the field of view of the camera, that the tracking accuracies of existing methods can be improved by increasing the resolution of the images, and that the tracking accuracy also depends on the quality of the camera calibration.

the tracking accuracy of existing monocular visual od-ometry methods is significantly worse than previously reported in the literature, and that the accuracy of these methods is highly sensitive to the type of camera motion and the environment.
